name: 1721 Prairie Avenue — Wirt Dexter house, Arthur Little's front of 1889, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D) with two curved bays on the Prairie face'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'Wirt Dexter Residence. Built 1863'. The house was remodelled later.

research_note: T-1878 (package N18A of T-1837) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under this id onto the K01 kit: the 1911 sheet's plan read against the 1891 Inland Architect plate of Arthur Little's front. T-1879 (package N18B) solves the plate's camera and works the front to it until the side-by-side matches: the bows' two lights a storey, the third floor's four lights and fanlight, the balustrades, shutters, ground-floor iron, the stack and the north flank. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1721-dexter-1878/README.md and docs/RESEARCH/k01-1721-dexter-1879/README.md are the reading.

documented_range.note: The 1891 plate shows Arthur Little's front of 1889; the 1911 sheet draws the same plan and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The c. 1888 photographs show the house before that front and are not this phase.

position.symbolic_location: 1721 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1721 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin carried 3.8 m north to the main block's north wall (the trace at draft v -3.75 to -3.9), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 1729.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1721-b1 p1) in the house's frame: its rear wall at u 0, the recessed wall behind the porch at u 7.7-7.75, its north wall at v 0 (the trace at -0.05 to 0.1 once carried), its south wall at v 17.6 (the trace at 17.6-17.8). The forward block, its bows and the rear wing stand on it (form.bays, form.rear_wings).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet; the 1891 plate shows three storeys over a low basement.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the main block and its rear wing brick. The plate shows the wall light and smooth.

principal_floor_m.note: The plate's porch stands six or so risers over the walk and its basement lights are at the walk: about 1.3 m.

storey_heights_m.note: Read off the plate in proportion to the porch's columns and the ground-floor windows: a tall principal storey, a second a little lower, a third under the cornice lower again.

service_wall_brick.note: A buff brick: the plate shows the walls light, much lighter than the red and brown brick of the houses beside it. Its exact colour is not read.

wall_finish.note: The plate draws every face light and smooth, with no brick courses on a print sharp enough to show the shutters' slats and the neighbours' brick, so the brick is taken as painted (or laid in a pale brick the kit does not carry). The plate is monochrome: the pale buff is chosen, not read.

street_front_trim.note: The plate's windows have small carved tablets over their heads; a cornice hood stands for them until T-1879 carves them.

wall_head.note: The plate's deep moulded cornice. Its modillions and the balustraded parapet over it are T-1879's.

roof_form.note: The plate shows no roof over the parapet from the street: a flat deck behind it.

eave_overhang_m.note: The plate's cornice stands well out of the wall.

window_kit.note: The kit's sash; the plate's windows are many-paned sash, T-1879's to glaze.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's floor fills the recess to the front's line, as the 1911 sheet draws the porch (2.9 m by 3.5 m) and the plate shows it.

stoop_width_m.note: The plate's steps run the porch's width between its columns.

entrance_bay.note: The door is in the recessed north part of the front (K01's low-v end: v runs south here, from the north wall), under the porch, on the plate.

front_bays.note: The recessed wall's one bay: the door, and a window over it in each upper storey (the plate).

value.head: plain
value.why_not_ordinary: the plate's small oval light on the north flank at the second floor (x 462-472, y 675-710 px), built as a square-headed light of the same size: K01 cuts no oval

value.head: plain
value.why_not_ordinary: the plate's narrow slot on the north flank at the principal floor (x 463-468, y 930-970 px)

side_bays.note: The north wall of the main block (K01's south wall in this house's frame), read off the 1891 plate through its solved camera (T-1879): one column of lights 4.0 m back from the front corner — a window at the third floor (x 460-475 px), a small oval light at the second (x 462-472 px; built square-headed at its size, K01 cutting no oval) and a narrow slot at the principal floor (x 463-468 px); the rest of the flank is blank wall in the plate. T-1878 had two columns at 2.0 and 5.75 m from the rules.

north_bays.note: The south wall toward 1729: no picture shows it.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall beside the rear wing: no picture shows it.

sash_by_storey.note: The plate's tall ground-floor and second-storey windows and the shorter third.

basement_lights.note: The plate's low basement lights at the walk.

chimneys.note: The plate's tall plain stack rising past the parapet at the forward block's north return, stood on the main block behind it; T-1879 sets its place (v 4.6 m) and its top (16.9 m) through the plate's solved camera, which shows its top about 3.5 m over the parapet. The second stack is the rules' and no picture shows it.

entrance_kit.note: The plate's porch: two round columns at its front corners, a flat roof under a deep fascia and cornice, railed as a balcony at the second floor, filling the recess to the front block's line. The rail is balustered on the plate; the kit's railing stands for it.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the principal storey's tall sash: the 1891 plate draws it taller than the lights above, so it is reconstructed 2.5 m clear in proportion to its 5.6 m storey, past K06's ordinary 2.4 m (T-1878)

bays.note: The 1911 sheet's front (trace s20fp-1721-b1 p1 in this frame): the forward block's face at u 10.6, 2.9 m before the recessed wall at u 7.7, from v 3.55 (its north return, beside the porch) to the south wall at v 17.6; the north bow from v 4.8 to 9.4, 1.2 m out, the south bow from v 12.6 to 17.0, 1.1 m out. The plate shows the block, both bows rising through the ground and second storeys and each roofed at the third floor (its balustrade is T-1879's); the windows' places on the bows and between them are read off the plate, their count to a face reconstructed. Each bow's outer lights stand 35 degrees round its curve from the middle one, which keeps their recesses in front of the forward block's face (at 40 they ran up to 0.09 m back onto it). T-1879, through the plate's solved camera: each bow has two lights a storey (at 33 degrees either side of its middle, a blank pier between them) and a stone balustrade round its top at the third floor; the forward block's third floor has a light over each side of each bow and a round-headed fanlight between them, and a stone balustrade along its parapet; every light but the fanlight has open louvred shutters, and the ground floor's lights iron guards on stone slabs, the centre one long enough that the three middle ones read as the plate's one run. Heights and the guards' and balusters' sizes are read in proportion; the shutters' colour and the balusters' square section are reconstructed (L-k01-1721-dress-1879).

rear_wings.note: The 1911 sheet's 'long 2B brick rear wing with 1-storey frame pieces at both ends' (census s20-1721-a1): the brick wing from the main rear wall to u -19.9, from the north wall (v 0) to v 6.2; the frame pieces at its east end (trace p3, p4) as one frame room to u -22.4. Its windows are reconstructed: no picture shows it.

window_shutters.note: The 1891 plate shows a pair of open louvred shutters folded back beside each upper light of the recessed front (x 545-685 px, both floors), dark against the light wall. Their colour is not shown (a monochrome plate): the deep green of T-2887's is reconstructed (docs/LIBERTIES.md, L-k01-1721-dress-1879). Inferred: their presence, count and places are the plate's, their widths read in proportion to the lights.

flat_balustrade.note: The 1891 plate shows the recessed front's parapet solid from the north-west corner for about 1.5 m (x 503-593 px through the solved camera), then turned balusters on a plinth under a rail to the forward block's return (x 593-705 px). The balusters are built square (the kit's bar), their turning not modelled. Inferred: the stretch is the plate's, the plinth, rail and balusters read in proportion.

boundary.note: T-3205 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The c. 1888 winter photograph shows a low squared stone coping along the street line, cut where the walk comes out from the house, a capped stone post standing either side of the cut about twice the coping's height (x 440-490 and 530-555 px); the 1891 plate's own coping is as low (its camera stands at grade, so its depth cannot be read off it). Built on the public walk's inner edge (the parcel's line, data/street_grid/1904.json prairie_1721, stands 0.1-0.2 m into the walk there), 0.4 m, the cut 1.8 m square to the stair with a 0.3 m post 0.9 m high either side. RECONSTRUCTED: the section, the cut's width and the posts' size (liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205).

grade_m.note: the app's ground over the house's lowest foot, measured in the published 1904 app (T-3205, tools/qa_house_walks_t3205.mjs): the yard is lifted onto it so the lawn and the walk are not under it

yard.note: T-3205 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The walk in flags from the stair's foot through the cut between the posts to the public walk, 1.5 m wide, and the lawn either side. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205. No turf is laid (lawn 'none'): the yard's grass is the app's own ground, as at 1720, which keeps the turf sheet (about 180 KB a house) out of the published tree, then at its 416 MB budget.
